title: A novel 7 RNA-based signature for prediction of prognosis in BRAF melanoma
author: Sun, Liu, et al.
materials: transcripts were expressed in all WT Bf-CM samples;

steps.title: Download and preprocess TCGA data
steps.instruction: Use the R package TCGAbiolinks to download transcriptional profiles, mutation data, and clinical information for 467 cutaneous melanoma (CM) patients from the TCGA‑SKCM project; exclude patients with BRAF somatic mutations and those lacking complete survival information, leaving 211 wild‑type BRAF CM (WT Bf‑CM) samples; split these 211 samples equally into a training set (n = 106) and a testing set (n = 105); extract NRAS and NF‑1 mutational statuses from the mutation data; download DNA methylation data for the same WT Bf‑CM patients using the R package cgdsr.

steps.title: Select RNAs based on expression criteria
steps.instruction: Align the RNA‑seq data to the human genome using the Gencode v22 annotation and quantify expression as Reads Per Kilobase per Million mapped reads (RPKM); retain only transcripts that are expressed in all WT Bf‑CM samples and have an average RPKM greater than 0.1; this yields a set of 14,202 RNAs for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Univariate Cox and select significant RNAs
steps.instruction: In the training set, perform univariate Cox regression for each of the 14,202 RNAs to assess association with overall survival (OS); keep RNAs with P‑value < 0.01, resulting in 251 candidate RNAs.

steps.title: Random forest variable selection and multivariate Cox
steps.instruction: Apply the randomForestSRC package to grow random‑forest models on the 251 survival‑related RNAs, repeatedly hunting variables and ranking them by frequency of occurrence; select the top 7 RNAs (the best OS‑relevant characteristics) and fit them into a stepped multivariate Cox regression model.

steps.title: Compute risk scores and define groups
steps.instruction: Calculate a risk score for each patient by weighting the expression levels of the 7 selected RNAs with their Cox coefficients; determine the median risk score in the training set and use it as a cutoff to classify patients in both training and testing sets into high‑risk and low‑risk groups.

steps.title: Survival analysis and ROC evaluation
steps.instruction: Perform Kaplan–Meier survival analysis using the survival package to compare high‑risk versus low‑risk groups; for WT Bf‑CM patients with at least 5‑year follow‑up, generate receiver‑operating characteristic (ROC) curves with the pROC package, compute area‑under‑the‑curve (AUC) values and 95 % confidence intervals to assess 5‑year OS prediction.

steps.title: Visualize risk scores and Cox results
steps.instruction: Order patients by scaled risk scores in descending order and create visualizations of risk scores, survival status, and expression of the 7 signature genes using ggplot2 and heatmap; display univariable and multivariable Cox analysis results with the forestplot package.

steps.title: Build nomogram and perform DCA
steps.instruction: Select three variables—signature risk score, patient age, and tumor stage—from the multivariable Cox analysis; integrate them into a predictive model for 3‑year and 5‑year survival; draw a nomogram with the rms package, evaluate its performance with concordance index (C‑index) and calibration curves, and conduct decision curve analysis (DCA) using the stdca script (https://github.com/matt-black/dcapy/blob/master/test/resource/stdca.R).

steps.title: Differential expression analysis between risk groups
steps.instruction: Using the edgeR package, compare gene expression between high‑risk and low‑risk groups; define differentially expressed genes (DEGs) as those with absolute log2FoldChange > 0.8 and adjusted P‑value < 0.001.

steps.title: Protein interaction network and core module identification
steps.instruction: Submit the 527 protein‑coding DEGs to the STRING database to obtain protein‑protein interaction (PPI) data; import the network into Cytoscape and apply the MCODE plugin to detect the highest‑scoring core module (M CODE score = 6).

steps.title: Functional enrichment and GSEA
steps.instruction: Perform Gene Ontology biological‑process (BP) enrichment of all DEGs and visualize clustered terms with the GOplot package; conduct Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) on MSigDB gene sets using the clusterProfiler package, reporting enriched sets such as GO_NUCLEAR_SPECK, GO_PYRIMIDINE_NUCLEOTIDE_BIOSYNTHETIC_PROCESS, REACTOME_MITOTIC_PROMETAPHASE, and TATA_01 with their normalized enrichment scores and P‑values.
